dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract

evidence.note: Early orientation was broad-but-shallow: surveyed skeleton types, Cargo/test files, but declared task impossible and defaulted to filling trivial methods from general knowledge rather than reconstructing Java semantics.
Committed to 'BreadthFirst traversal from highest-degree nodes' for default layout as an assumption about BioFabric conventions rather than reading the Java layout class first.

After an EDA byte-diff, opened DefaultEdgeLayout.java and traced the actual comparator (reg-vs-shadow tie-breaks, top/bot row ordering) before rewriting the edge sort — genuine Java reconstruction driven by a diff.

Deep, precise reconstruction of Java color math: HSB→RGB rounding with float32 precision, brighter/darker channel transforms, DEFAULT_NODE_LIGHTER_LEVEL=0.43, cross-checked against exact golden RGB bytes. Level-10 quality for this component.
NID assignment, drain zones, and alignment ordering were inferred by staring at golden files rather than traced from Java source, encoding golden-fit behavior instead of recovered semantics.
Multiple specialized layouts (similarity, set, control_top, world_bank, cluster) were stubbed to delegate to default without reading their Java counterparts — no orientation for those subsystems.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reads relevant Java classes and goldens for several components before/while coding them (level 5), and for two subsystems — edge sort and color generation — it systematically traces Java call paths and identifies subtle byte-divergence sources like float32 rounding and brighter/darker transforms, returning to the reference when diffs demand it (level 8-10 traits). But this rigor is not sustained across the whole horizon: initial orientation was shallow with an impossibility framing, the core default layout was assumed rather than verified, and NID/drain-zone/alignment behavior plus many stubbed layouts were golden-inferred rather than Java-traced. This mix of one or two deep, self-correcting reconstructions against broad guessing/stubbing places the observed level at 6.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones

evidence.note: Assessed the large coupled scope and decided to start with foundational data-model methods before algorithm-heavy pieces — dependency awareness at the outset.
Tackled analysis first, explicitly because it was 'simpler' than parity; used cargo test --test analysis_tests as the completion signal for that grouping.
Moved to CLI commands as a coherent grouping and used cli_tests pass/fail as the done-check (50/51 passing) before advancing.
Recognized parity tests were blocked by todo!() in runners.rs and sequenced implementing runners.rs to unblock the parity test group — dependency-aware unblocking.

Deferred harder components (BIF serialization, alignment merge) to later, tackling NOA/EDA before BIF, and alignment last; but handled newly-revealed alignment coupling reactively rather than revising an explicit plan.
Final tally reported per test group (CLI/lib/analysis/parity/pipeline), reflecting that milestones were organized by test suite throughout.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently grouped work by component/test suite and progressed in a sensible dependency order (model → parsers → analysis → alignment → layout → CLI → parity runners), each grouping closed by a runnable test group as its done-check — squarely matching anchor 5, with the extra dependency reasoning (choosing 'simpler/foundational' groupings first and unblocking parity via runners.rs) pushing above it. It falls short of 8 because there was no explicit upfront milestone plan defining each milestone by a predefined test set; the sequencing was emergent and the numerous 'Plan:' lines were mostly tactical navigation, and coupling discoveries were handled reactively rather than through plan revision. Hence a 6.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification

evidence.note: Used focused test invocation (sif_triangle_eda) plus 'First diff' byte inspection to pinpoint edge-ordering divergence, then cross-referenced Java DefaultEdgeLayout sort to fix — diff-driven localization.

Ran diff of golden vs golden-noshadow to discover shadows are still present, distinguishing a format assumption (strip shadows) from actual behavior; iteratively verified line counts (16 vs 31) to confirm root cause.

Built auxiliary python probes computing float32 HSB→RGB, cross-validated against Java reference source (ColorGenerator, DEFAULT_NODE_LIGHTER_LEVEL=0.43) to derive the exact brighter/darker transform matching golden RGB bytes — algorithmic vs format isolation via targeted probes.
Reproduced BIF mismatch on minimal isolated_nodes input, diffed NID values, and identified nid must be input-order not row-order — ordering-vs-format distinction on smallest input.
Recognized that stub layouts coincidentally matched default output and that link-group configs were ignored by the runner — showing green tests were scrutinized rather than trusted blindly.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's process squarely matches the level-8 anchor: it drove every component from focused test invocations and byte-level 'First diff' inspection, and constructed genuine auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, standalone float32 color computations, hand-verified RGB) to separate formatting from algorithmic causes. It exceeds 5 clearly and touches level-10 traits by cross-validating color and edge-sort logic against the actual Java reference and noticing when green tests didn't exercise the real path. It stops short of a full layered 10 because coverage was incomplete with abandoned surfaces and it did not systematically confirm every passing test exercised the intended code path.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface

evidence.note: Continuous net-count tracking with explicit deltas ('40 passed up from 32', '58 passing 5 failures left'), establishing a running ledger early.
Distinguishes a genuinely-solved pass from a coincidental one — questions why alignment tests passed and checks golden values (EC=0.689 not 0) rather than trusting the green.
Whole-suite re-runs producing per-group counts (51 CLI, 13 lib, 58 analysis, 160/388 total) — maintains an accurate live picture across the large test surface.

Categorizes remaining failures by group (BIF, specialized layouts, link-grouping, roundtrip) and deliberately defers stubborn ones ('skip these for now', 'give up on BIF... don't regress') instead of looping.

Abandons drainZone/BIF as 'far too complex' then later returns with a productive angle (color brighten/darken), showing tactic-change rather than pure thrashing; counts jump 60->77 confirming the ledger.
At the end the suite hangs; agent loses clean live accounting and waits blindly across many turns, though it retains its last-known state (85 parity / ~209 total).

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintains an explicit, continuously-updated ledger of pass counts with 'up from X' deltas, categorizes remaining failures per test group, re-runs the whole suite to confirm progress, and even distinguishes coincidental passes from genuine ones (step 61-62) — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and touching level-10 traits (deliberate deferral of stubborn diffs, coincidence detection). It falls short of a 10 because the failure set improved near-monotonically so it never had to catch a regression of a green case, and it lost clean live accounting during the terminal test-hang (steps 271-292). Net behavior sits solidly at 8.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions

evidence.note: Triangle EDA byte-diff falsified the edge-ordering assumption. Rather than tweaking output, the agent opened Java DefaultEdgeLayout.java, read the actual comparator (steps 165-167), derived the real rules (both-regular sort by top/bot, both-shadow by bot/top, reg-vs-shadow tie goes to shadow), and rewrote the general edge sort — fixing a whole class of EDA tests (36→49).

noshadow EDA diff (16 vs 31 lines) revealed the assumption that shadows=false strips shadows was wrong. Agent diffed goldens, saw shadows still present, traced it to include_shadows flag, and corrected the general layout behavior rather than special-casing individual tests.

Strongest example: BIF color diff (g=217 vs computed 152). Agent did NOT hardcode the golden value. It verified its HSB->RGB math in Python, concluded the golden came from a different spec, traced through Java ColorGenerator to discover nodes use a BRIGHTER transform (channel*1.43) and links a DARKER transform (*0.6993) with useHSV=false, verified the formula against both node and link goldens, and applied the general transform — resolving a family of BIF tests (60→77).

self-loop drain-zone and nid-assignment diffs each traced to root cause (self-loops belong in drain zone; nid = input insertion order, not row index) and fixed generally, each unlocking multiple tests (79→85).

Some symptom-patching present: minimal BIF stub crafted to contain 'xml'/'node' for a CLI test, and a perfect-alignment-self NGS/LGS/JS=1.0 special case — brittle fixes that don't reflect returning to the Java model.

Alignment-layout diff correctly diagnosed (default BFS ordering wrong vs Java NetworkAlignmentLayout degree-group ordering) but the component was ultimately left unfixed amid test hangs/scope, so correction was not carried through everywhere.

dimensions.reasoning: Across the trajectory the agent repeatedly treated a stubborn byte-diff as evidence of a wrong model and returned to the Java source to find the real rule (edge comparator, brighter/darker color transform, nid ordering, drain-zone semantics), refactoring general logic rather than hardcoding — squarely the level-8 pattern, with the color investigation touching level-10 by resolving a whole family of failing cases from one corrected formula. It falls short of a clean 10 because a few brittle special-cases and CLI stubs appear, and some components (alignment/specialized layouts) were abandoned rather than corrected. Net: a strong 8.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens

evidence.note: Read Java DefaultEdgeLayout to derive the general edge-sort comparator (top/bot row, reg-vs-shadow tie rule) rather than fitting the triangle EDA output.

When a color channel mismatched the golden, refused to fit the value; traced Java ColorGenerator/getHSBColor and NODE_LIGHTER_LEVEL to derive the general brighter (*1.43 capped) / darker (/1.43) formulas and cross-verified on the link-darker case — strong faithful-porting discipline.

Golden-specific shortcut: scoring special-cased perfect-vs-self alignment to return 1.0 instead of the real NodeGroupMap classification; agent itself noted it wrongly returns 1.0 for non-perfect cases (won't generalize).
Specialized layouts (similarity/set/control_top/world_bank/cluster) stubbed to default-ish output rather than ported — incomplete generalization for those components.
Derived nid assignment as a general rule (node input-insertion order) from reasoning about Java behavior, verified against golden as a check.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent overwhelmingly implemented general logic derived from the actual Java reference (edge sort, HSB color math with brighter/darker factors, nid ordering, drain zones), using goldens as checks not targets — the color-derivation episode is textbook anchor-8 behavior where it refused to fit an output and instead found the underlying reference formula. This is offset by one clearly acknowledged golden-specific shortcut (perfect-vs-self scoring → 1.0) and several layouts stubbed to default output rather than faithfully ported, which are the 'lean on golden-specific assumptions in places' of anchor 3. The blend of faithful, self-checking porting for most components with a few recognized shortcuts places it just above the anchor-5 midpoint.

rubric.task_read: A very long-horizon, high-complexity port: reimplement a Java network-visualization tool (BioFabric) plus its alignment plugin as a Rust library and CLI, achieving BYTE-LEVEL parity with the Java reference across many file formats, layout algorithms, and serialization paths, with a fixed public API and a held-out test suite. Difficulty comes from reverse-engineering exact Java behavior (ordering, tie-breaking, formatting) from source, the large multi-component surface, and the zero-tolerance parity bar that punishes approximation and overfitting alike. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in reference-reading, sequencing across components, golden-diff-driven verification, and disciplined faithful porting rather than pattern-matching to visible goldens.

dimensions.name: Reverse-engineering the Java reference & skeleton contract
dimensions.description: Reading the Java BioFabric/AlignmentPlugin source and the Rust skeleton deeply enough to reproduce exact algorithms, ordering, and output formats before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Byte-level parity is impossible without recovering the precise semantics (layout order, tie-breaking, number/string formatting, file structure) that live only in the Java source; acting from guesses about network-viz conventions guarantees off-by-format failures.

anchors.0: Starts filling in todo!() from general knowledge of graph layout with no visible reading of the Java reference or the skeleton's types/golden formats.
anchors.3: Skims one or two Java files or the Rust signatures; grabs surface structure but misses ordering/formatting details, so implementations encode guessed behavior.
anchors.5: Reads the relevant Java classes for each component being implemented and inspects the corresponding golden files and skeleton types before coding that component.
anchors.8: Systematically traces the Java call paths for each subsystem (parsing, layout, serialization, alignment), extracting exact iteration order, comparators, and formatting rules, and cross-checks them against golden bytes and skeleton signatures before committing to an approach.
anchors.10: Sustained, precise reconstruction of Java semantics: identifies subtle sources of byte divergence (stable-sort tie-breaks, locale/precision in number formatting, insertion-order maps, whitespace/line-ending conventions) directly from source, builds a mental/written model of the format contract, and returns to the reference whenever a new component or diff demands it.

dimensions.name: Sequencing components into verifiable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the port into an ordered set of sub-goals (formats/parsers → core model → layout → serialization → alignment → CLI) each with a concrete done-check tied to a test group.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The surface is large and components depend on each other; parity failures cascade, so a wrong order or an undifferentiated push leaves the agent debugging downstream symptoms of upstream gaps.

anchors.0: No visible ordering; jumps between unrelated functions/tests reactively as failures appear.
anchors.3: A vague intention to 'implement things and pass tests' with little dependency awareness; milestones aren't tied to checks.
anchors.5: Groups work by test suite/component and tackles them in a sensible dependency order, each grouping ending with a runnable test.
anchors.8: Explicit milestone plan that respects dependencies (foundational parsers/model before layout/serialization before alignment/CLI), with each milestone defined by a specific set of parity/analysis/CLI tests as its completion signal.
anchors.10: A dependency-aware plan that isolates high-risk parity-sensitive pieces early, sequences so that each milestone unblocks and de-risks the next, and is revised as reverse-engineering reveals hidden coupling — turning a sprawling port into a controlled progression.

dimensions.name: Golden-diff-driven parity verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the parity/analysis/CLI tests and byte-level diffing to confirm correctness, and building finer-grained checks when a whole-file diff is too coarse to localize a mismatch.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The bar is exact-match, so success is defined by the golden diffs; a strong agent drives implementation from these checks and manufactures visibility into WHERE bytes diverge rather than assuming a passing compile means correctness.

anchors.0: Implements without running the parity tests, or treats compilation as success.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads pass/fail counts but doesn't inspect the actual byte differences to diagnose failures.
anchors.5: Runs targeted tests per component and examines golden-vs-actual diffs to guide fixes.
anchors.8: Uses focused test invocations and byte-level diff inspection to pinpoint exact divergences, and constructs auxiliary checks (minimal inputs, intermediate-output comparisons, hex/whitespace inspection) to isolate formatting vs. algorithmic causes.
anchors.10: A layered verification regime: reproduces each mismatch on the smallest input, distinguishes format-level from ordering-level from algorithmic errors via targeted probes, cross-validates against the Java reference's actual behavior where feasible, and treats every green test as evidence only after confirming it exercises the real path — leaving essentially no unverified surface.

dimensions.name: Tracking pass/fail across a large test surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which test groups pass vs. remain, and detecting when byte-diff debugging has become circular.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With many parity cases and a zero-tolerance bar, it is easy to lose the plot, re-fix the same diff repeatedly, or believe progress that regressions have undone; an accurate ledger sustains forward motion over the long horizon.

anchors.0: No sense of overall status; fixes things without knowing net pass count or whether earlier passes still hold.
anchors.3: Occasional full-suite runs but no tracking of which cases remain or whether fixes caused regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a working list of remaining failures and periodically re-runs the whole suite to catch regressions.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, updated ledger of done-vs-remaining per test group, notices when a fix regresses a previously-green case, and flags when repeated attempts at one diff aren't converging.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the whole horizon: distinguishes genuinely-solved from flaky/coincidental passes, catches thrashing on a stubborn byte-diff early and deliberately changes tactic or defers, and never loses track of net progress even as the failure set churns.

dimensions.name: Correcting course when byte-diffs falsify assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach and mental model of Java behavior when a parity diff reveals the current assumption is wrong, rather than patching symptoms.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Reverse-engineering inevitably produces wrong hypotheses about ordering/formatting; the effective agent treats a persistent diff as a signal to return to the reference and fix the root model, not to bolt on special-cases that break held-out tests.

anchors.0: Keeps forcing the same approach against a failing diff, or abandons a component when the obvious fix fails.
anchors.3: Makes local tweaks in response to diffs but rarely revisits the underlying assumption that produced them.
anchors.5: When a fix doesn't work, re-reads the relevant Java code and adjusts the approach to match observed behavior.
anchors.8: Treats a stubborn diff as evidence of a wrong model, traces back to the Java source to find the real rule (comparator, format, edge case), and refactors the general logic rather than hardcoding the specific case.
anchors.10: Systematically converts falsified assumptions into corrected general understanding: distinguishes a one-off from a class of errors, updates the format/algorithm model once so a family of failing cases resolves together, and resists brittle special-casing that would pass visible goldens but fail held-out inputs.

dimensions.name: Faithful porting vs. overfitting to visible goldens
dimensions.description: Choosing to implement the general Java algorithm so held-out cases pass, rather than reverse-fitting output to the specific visible golden files.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A held-out suite over unseen networks means any hardcoding or golden-specific shortcut that passes visible tests will fail grading; the meta-decision to port faithfully is a distinct discipline this task specifically rewards.

anchors.0: Hardcodes or special-cases outputs to match visible goldens (e.g. keying on known inputs), guaranteeing held-out failures.
anchors.3: Implements mostly general logic but leans on golden-specific assumptions (fixed sizes, sample-specific ordering) in places.
anchors.5: Implements the general algorithm for each component, using goldens as checks rather than as targets to fit.
anchors.8: Deliberately generalizes from the Java source's actual logic, actively avoids input-specific shortcuts, and sanity-checks that logic would hold for inputs beyond the provided samples.
anchors.10: Consistently prioritizes a faithful port of the reference algorithms, explicitly reasons about which behaviors must generalize and stress-tests its implementation against edge cases not present in the visible goldens, treating byte-parity on samples as necessary-but-insufficient evidence of a correct general port.
